title: Advanced Characterization and Modeling of Microstructure in Irradiated UO2
content: Advancing the understanding and predictive modeling of microstructural evolution in nuclear fuel is essential for accelerating the development and deployment of robust fuels and advanced reactor designs. During reactor operation, UO2 fuels undergo significant microstructural and chemical transformations. Some fission products remain dissolved in the UO2 matrix as solid solutions, while inert gases such as xenon and krypton, along with 4d transition metals—including molybdenum, technetium, ruthenium, rhodium, and palladium—form bubbles and metallic precipitates. Additionally, grain subdivision within the reactor environment results in the formation of nano-sized grains at high burn-up levels.
